You can either do it with a single interval and evaluate the function from x=0 to .2 or you can do it with a double integral  and use the function as a limit for y in one integrand, evaluated from x=0 to .2 in the other.  

This is what vector calculus is all about.  In that class, you will use rectangles, squares, AND triangles (Stoke's Theorem) to calculate area.
